title: Working with AI: Measuring the Applicability of Generative AI to Occupations
claim: Real-world usage is concentrated in a few information-work activities, and AI actions differ from user goals and from workforce activity.
layout: 3 panels: two stacked bar charts left, one tall bar chart right
description: Three horizontal bar-chart panels analyze the frequency of work activities in Bing Copilot conversations. On the left, two stacked panels show the top 15 intermediate work activities as user goals (top) and as AI actions (bottom). Bars are colored by category: red for Learn, green for Communicate, purple for Teach/Explain, orange for Write, and black for Other. Thin dividers and right-aligned category labels separate the groups. Panel C, on the right, is a tall chart of about 35 generalized work activities. Each row has a solid bar for user goal, a hatched bar for AI action, and a small black tick for workforce frequency. The eye goes first to the long red 'Get Information' bar at about 0.42 and the long hatched green communication bars. A legend sits at the bottom right.
caption: Frequency of work activities in Bing Copilot usage. (A) The 15 IWAs that occur most frequently as user goals. (B) The 15 IWAs that occur most frequently as AI actions. (C) The frequencies of GWAs as user goals and AI actions, compared to a rough estimate of GWA workforce frequency (described in Section B). All panels show researcher-generated IWA groupings.
abstract: With generative AI emerging as a general-purpose technology, understanding its economic effects is among society's most pressing questions. Earlier work on AI impact largely relied on predictions of AI capabilities or focused narrowly on individual firms. Drawing instead on real-world AI usage, we analyze a dataset of 200k anonymized conversations with Microsoft Bing Copilot to measure AI applicability to occupations. We use an LLM-based pipeline to classify the O*NET work activities assisted or performed by AI in each conversation. We find that the most common and successful AI-assisted work activities involve information work--the creation, processing, and communication of information. At the occupation level, we find widespread AI applicability cutting across sectors, as most occupations have information work components. Our methodology also allows us to predict which occupations are more likely to delegate tasks to AI and which are more likely to use AI to assist existing workflows. Finally, we see an increase in occupation-level AI applicability over our 9-month data period, driven primarily by people using AI for more varied tasks. AI applicability scores and component usage and success metrics are available at https://github.com/microsoft/working-with-ai.
